page: Microsoft Azure E20ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon 8272CL processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 20 vCPUs across 10 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 160.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive operations. Local storage consists of an integrated 805 GB solid-state drive (SSD) alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include a graphics processing unit (GPU).

In standardized computing benchmarks, the E20ds_v4 demonstrates consistent mid-tier performance across both single-threaded and multi-threaded evaluations. The processor achieved a PassMark CPU score of 19266.4 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 7921.0. Memory subsystems deliver an uncached read bandwidth of 80.0 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 41.59 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput memory operations such as Redis SET benchmarks at 17.23 million operations per second. However, machine learning inference displays limitations; text generation on small models (71.75 tokens/sec) and prompt processing on 7B parameter models (30.52 tokens/sec) fall within the lower quartile of comparative benchmarks.

The hardware profile offers a balanced cost efficiency for memory-centric enterprise deployments, avoiding the expense of dedicated GPU accelerators while bundling high-capacity local temporary SSD space. The combination of 160 GB RAM, AVX-512 vector support, and dedicated CPU threading positions the E20ds_v4 effectively for in-memory caching layers, relational database servers, business analytics processing, and enterprise application hosting.
